title.narrative: Delhi-Meerut Regional Rapid Transit System Investment Project - Tranche 1

description.narrative: The Delhi-Meerut Regional Rapid Transit System (RRTS) Project will finance a new, dedicated, high-capacity, rail-based commuter transit corridor. The estimated 82 kilometer (km)-long corridor will pass through the densely populated sections of the National Capital Region (NCR) connecting Delhi to Meerut via Ghaziabad. The project will finance rail track, signaling, electrical and mechanical works, station buildings and maintenance facilities. The project will also support capacity and institutional development for setting up an operation and maintenance organization. The first tranche of the MFF will cover the initial civil works, including construction of viaducts for part of the elevated section of the corridor and a depot. Other contracts for underground sections, track works, traction, signaling etc. will be awarded in quick succession and the remaining tranches will gradually fund these contracts, as they progress.

description.narrative: Efficiency, safety, social inclusiveness, and environmental sustainability of transport in the Delhi-Meerut regional rapid transit system (RRTS) corridor improved
258,035 tons of carbon dioxide reduced per annum Progress/Status: To be measured after project completion Data Source: NCRTC statistics Actual value:
Travel time between Delhi and Meerut by train reduced to 1 hour Progress/Status: To be measured after project completion Data Source: NCRTC statistics Actual value:

At least 70% of riders, including elderly, women, children and differently abled, perceive the RRTS to be accessible, safe, and reliable Progress/Status: To be measured after project completion Data Source: RRTS user survey by NCRTC Base year: 2020 Baseline value: N
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Indicator Indicator: 32% progress towards at least five RRTS stations developed as major multimodal hubs Progress/Status: Multimodal integration of RRTS is substantially completed and operational at Anand Vihar, New Ashok Nagar, Sahibabad, and Ghaziabad RRTS stations. Data Source: Progress reports Actual value:

Output: Indicator Indicator: At least 200 differently-abled persons received hearing, visual and/or physical mobility assistive aids Progress/Status: Partly completed. 197 have been distributed, while NCRTC is procuring about 675 assistive aides Data Source: Progress and completion reports submitted to ADB and NCRTC by the contracted organization, including certificates issued upon completion of trainings and/or receipt of assistive aids Actual value:

Output: Indicator Indicator: At least 200 women received training for employment and/or entrepreneurial opportunities arising from improved RRTS corridors Progress/Status: Completed. Around 1,407 women received training for employment and/or entrepreneurial opportunities arising from improved RRTS corridors. This includes 500 women trained in self-employed tailoring, 407 girls provided vocational skills, and 500 women and girls provided e-mobility (e-rickshaw and car driving) trainings. Data Source: Progress and completion reports submitted to ADB and NCRTC by the contracted organization, including certificates issued upon completion of trainings and/or receipt of assistive aids Actual value:

Output: Institutional capacity of the NCRTC strengthened Indicator: 32% progress towards 82 route-kilometers of standard gauge electrified rail track installed, with systems and signaling Progress/Status: Out of 82 km of RRTS corridor, 55km section from New Ashok Nagar to Meerut South is operational, covering 11 stations. Civil works between Sarai Kale Khan and Modipuram are complete with CMRS approval, and finishing works and trials are underway, while works on the Modipuram-Depot and Sarai Kale Khan-Jangpura stretches are ongoing. The overall physical progress of the project is 95.9% upto Sept 2025. Data Source: Progress reports Actual value:

Output: Mobility and economic opportunities of women and differently abled improved Indicator: 32% progress towards 24 elderly, women, children, differently abled-friendly stations with climate- and disaster-resilient features constructed and operational Progress/Status: Ongoing. EWCD-friendly and climate- and disaster resilient features have been built into the project design. Data Source: Progress reports Actual value:
